 Sign in Hybrid Rugby Players: A Test History
 All Blacks 23 hours ago By:   Alan Brown Antoine Dupont's move to first five-eighth for France this weekend puts versatility back in the spotlight, but the All Blacks have a long history of versatile players too Antoine Dupont will start at first five-eighth for France against South Africa in Paris this weekend, one of the most talked-about selections of the Nations Championship .
 The All Blacks will head into their own Test in Cardiff with a hybrid player of their own in Leicester Fainga'anuku , while the Springboks have made the concept a feature of their match-day squads. But players covering more than one position is nothing new in the black jersey.
 Dupont shifts to No.10 in Paris
 France head coach Fabien Galthié confirmed the move on 11 November 2026, with his four leading options at first five-eighth unavailable: Romain Ntamack, Matthieu Jalibert, Antoine Hastoy and Thomas Ramos.
 Ntamack dislocated his shoulder in France's 54-17 win over Fiji in Lyon. Maxime Lucu, who covered first five-eighth in that match, will instead start at halfback, with Dupont moving out one position.
 It is reported to be Dupont's first Test start at first five-eighth.
 France v South Africa, 14 November 2026 at Stade de France, Paris (9.10am NZDT)
 Watch: Crusaders Legend | Leicester Fainga'anuku
 Crusaders Legend | Leicester Fainga'anuku Leicester Fainga'anuku: the All Blacks' hybrid
 Leicester Fainga'anuku was named as a loose forward in the All Blacks' 36-man squad for the Nations Championship Northern Series. Head coach Dave Rennie has described his role as "definitely hybrid", with the 27-year-old able to cover wing, second five-eighth and openside flanker.
 Fainga'anuku has 12 Test caps, many of them on the wing. After two seasons with Toulon, where he added scrummaging to his game, he returned to the Crusaders in 2026 and started at openside flanker for the final six matches of the Super Rugby Pacific season.
 His most recent Test came against Wales in Cardiff in November 2025, when he came off the bench wearing the No.22 jersey.
 WATCH: Rivals: The Podcast | Jim Hamilton: Is Henry Pollock the Next Ardie? JK & Victor CLASH Over Hybrid Players
 Rivals: The Podcast | Jim Hamilton: Is Henry Pollock the Next Ardie? JK & Victor CLASH Over Hybrid Players The Springbok approach
 South Africa have made versatility a regular feature of their match-day squads under Rassie Erasmus, often pairing a forward-heavy bench with players who can move between the forwards and backs.
 Kwagga Smith
 A loose forward who has played all three back-row positions, Smith has also covered the wing when the Springboks have named six forwards and two backs on the bench.
 André Esterhuizen
 South Africa 54, Barbarians 7 , Cape Town, 28 June 2025
 The 1.93m, 115kg centre made his first appearance at flanker in the Springboks' season opener against the Barbarians, with Erasmus describing him afterwards as a hybrid player. Five months later in Paris, after Lood de Jager was sent off, Esterhuizen helped 14-man South Africa to a 32-17 win over France, scoring from a rolling maul.
 Two jerseys, one All Black
 The term hybrid may be new, but All Blacks selectors have long valued players who could be trusted in more than one role.
 Jon Preston 
 Halfback and first five-eighth, 1991 to 1997 
 Preston represented Canterbury and Wellington and toured the 1991 Rugby World Cup, making his Test debut against the USA in Gloucester. He played 27 matches for the All Blacks, including 10 Tests, and his goal-kicking added to his value. He scored a try in the deciding third Test against the British & Irish Lions in 1993.
 Piri Weepu 
 Halfback and first five-eighth, 2004 to 2013 
 Weepu was first and foremost a halfback, but his work at first five-eighth for the Hurricanes made him a valued option at No.10. He filled in at first five-eighth against the Springboks in 2011 and, at that year's Rugby World Cup, took over the goal-kicking duties for the quarter-final against Argentina after Dan Carter was ruled out of the tournament.
 Watch: All Black #1049 | Piri Weepu
 All Black #1049 | Piri Weepu All Blacks v Namibia, Rugby World Cup 2019
 All Blacks 71-9 Namibia, 6 October 2019 at Tokyo Stadium, Tokyo
 The closest recent parallel to Dupont's switch came in the pool stage of Rugby World Cup 2019. Jordie Barrett started at first five-eighth against Namibia, and in the second half halfback TJ Perenara moved out to No.10, with Brad Weber taking over at halfback.
 Watch: 2019, World Cup | New Zealand v Namibia
 2019, World Cup | New Zealand v Namibia More All Blacks who have covered more than one role
 Colin Meads : Made his Test debut at flanker in 1957 and, in the second Test against Australia in Brisbane that year, moved to the wing after Frank McMullen was injured, scoring his first Test try.
 Michael Jones : Moved from openside to blindside flanker later in his career.
 Eric Rush : A flanker in his early career who played on the wing for the All Blacks.
 Tana Umaga : Began his All Blacks career on the wing before moving into the midfield, playing both centre and second five-eighth and later captaining the national side.
 Christian Cullen : The fullback was used at centre at the 1999 Rugby World Cup.
 Dan Carter : Played six Tests at second five-eighth before establishing himself at first five-eighth.
 Isaia Toeava : One of the All Blacks' most versatile backs, Toeava appeared in Tests across the midfield, on the wing and at fullback, and also had an appearance at first five-eighth.
 Jerome Kaino : The blindside flanker started at lock against Ireland in Chicago in 2016.
 Beauden Barrett : World Player of the Year at first five-eighth in 2016 and 2017, he played almost all of the 2019 Rugby World Cup at fullback.
 Jordie Barrett : Started Tests at first five-eighth (v Namibia, Rugby World Cup 2019), on both wings and at fullback before settling at second five-eighth.
 Scott Barrett : The lock has started at blindside flanker, including the 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final against England.
 Damian McKenzie : Has moved between fullback and first five-eighth throughout his Test career, including in 2026.
 WATCH: The Final Interview: Sir Colin Meads
 The Final Interview: Sir Colin Meads The tradition continues
 From Preston and Weepu to the Barrett brothers, the All Blacks have regularly called on players who can cover more than one role. The difference today is that hybrid players are increasingly selected by design, giving coaches greater flexibility in how they build their match-day 23.
 That will be on show this weekend in both Paris and Cardiff:
 France v South Africa, 14 November 2026 at Stade de France, Paris (9.10am NZDT)
 Wales v All Blacks, 15 November 2026 at Principality Stadium, Cardiff (3.10am NZDT) 
 A note on 1937 and 1956
 Positional switches against the Springboks are not new for the All Blacks. In the first Test against South Africa in 1937, loose forward Ron Ward moved to the wing after injuries in the backline. Nineteen years later, in the third Test of the 1956 series, flanker Bill Clark shifted to centre when Robin Archer was injured, in a series the All Blacks went on to win.
